document.title: Policy on Track, But Violence Will Rise (Kabul 000746)
document.authors: U.S. Embassy Kabul (Ambassador Ronald E. Neumann)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), "No-Go" Tribal Areas Became Basis for Afghan Insurgency Documents Show
document.note: [Secret] Neumann says violence is rising as the Taliban adopt lethal guerrilla and suicide-bomb tactics and ISAF moves into Helmand, but this does not indicate a failing policy. The insurgency is strengthening because of four years of reorganizing in a sanctuary beyond the reach of Kabul or Islamabad. Left unaddressed, this sanctuary will bring back the strategic threat that prompted OEF. He sees more Pakistani pressure on the Taliban but doubts Pakistani capabilities.

key_claims: Violence in Afghanistan will rise through the coming months, including suicide bombs in Kabul and attacks on ISAF.
The shift to IEDs and suicide bombs reflects the failure of Taliban large-unit tactics in 2005 as much as increased threat.
The Taliban reorganized for four years in a sanctuary beyond either government's reach, which will prolong the insurgency if unaddressed.
Without addressing sanctuary, the strategic threat that prompted OEF could re-emerge.
Pakistan is applying more pressure on the Taliban, but concerns remain about its capabilities.
Extending provincial governance is essential to counter the Taliban's long-term strategy of keeping the government weak.
